title: Verifier‑Augmented Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) to Prevent Unsafe Network Configurations — Preregistered Reparations
research_question: Does integrating a deterministic network verifier into an LLM-driven generate–verify–repair loop reduce the rate of safety‑violating network configurations compared to LLM-only generation?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: An LLM+verifier GVR loop produces a lower proportion of configurations that violate the preregistered safety property set than LLM-only single‑pass generation (paired comparison).
H0: There is no difference in the proportion of safety violations between LLM+verifier GVR and LLM-only generation.
exploratory_questions: EQ1: What is the distribution of repair iterations required before the verifier accepts a configuration?
EQ2: What failure modes remain (verifier false negatives, unresolved repairs, verifier-induced brittle repairs)?
EQ3: How do different verifier property‑sets (strict vs. permissive) change the tradeoff between safety violations and successful repair convergence?
benchmark_scope: Intent-to-configuration tasks derived from public NetOps task templates and configuration snippets (public datasets and templates only).
Safety properties defined over reachability, ACL semantics, and default-route constraints as implemented in the chosen verifier(s).
model_scope: Hosted LLM API (single hosted LLM endpoint is used for all generation/repair calls; exact endpoint identifier will be recorded in execution manifest).
transformation_scope: Normalization and canonicalization of generated configs (AST normalization), placeholder substitution, and semantic-equivalence checks prior to verifier invocation.
primary_estimand: Paired difference in safety‑violation rate: proportion of tasks with final configurations violating the preregistered safety property set under LLM-only generation minus that under LLM+verifier GVR.
secondary_estimands: Absolute and relative reduction in violation rate (percentage points and percent change).
Distribution (mean, median, IQR) of repair iterations to first verifier pass.
Proportion of tasks where GVR fails to reach a verifier‑passing config within max iterations.
sampling_plan: Paired-task design. N = 400 independent intent-to-configuration tasks sampled from public NetOps templates and synthetic variations derived deterministically from those templates (no human annotation). Inclusion criteria: tasks must be representable as an intent that maps to a single configuration fragment (routing/ACL/interface settings). Exclusion: tasks requiring vendor‑private features or proprietary data. Task clusters: 4 difficulty clusters (simple ACL/routing change, moderate intent translation, multi‑device change, multi‑policy constraints). Confirmatory items (paired tasks) = 400 (100 per cluster). Discovery/exploratory items = 0 additional confirmatory tasks; exploratory analyses use the same N=400 and prespecified subgroup analyses.
analysis_plan: Primary test: McNemar's test on paired binary outcomes (violation/no violation) with α = 0.05. Report paired absolute difference and 95% CI (Agresti‑Coull method). Secondary: bootstrap 95% CIs for iterations distribution, report effect sizes (risk difference, relative risk). Predefine subgroup analyses by task cluster; label subgroup results as exploratory if not powered. Predefine handling of technical failures: if an execution failure occurs for a task in either condition, mark task as 'technical failure' and exclude pair from primary McNemar analysis; report number and reasons for exclusions and perform sensitivity analysis counting these as violations in either or both arms.
multiplicity_plan: Primary confirmatory test is a single paired McNemar comparison (no multiplicity adjustment). Prespecified secondary and subgroup analyses are exploratory; report unadjusted p-values and confidence intervals and label accordingly.
missingness_plan: Record full execution manifest. Pairs with any technical failure (API outage, verifier crash, runtime error) will be excluded from the primary paired test and reported in a pre-registered exclusion table. Sensitivity analyses: (1) treat excluded pairs as violations in both arms; (2) treat excluded pairs as violations only in LLM-only arm; (3) multiple imputation is not allowed because no human annotation is permitted.

benchmark_names: Public NetOps intent templates (curated set derived from public teaching labs and RFC‑style examples)
risk_factors: LLM overfitting to verifier behavior (producing syntactic fixes that pass the verifier but are operationally brittle)
Verifier blind spots (false negatives) giving false safety signal
Cross-task leakage if deterministic template derivation reuses identifiers
detection_procedures: Semantic-equivalence AST checks to detect syntactic evasion (normalization + AST compare).
Verifier false‑negative estimation via unit tests (verifier‑missed injected-bug cases; see verifier validation below).
Random 5% automated audit: re-run accepted configs under an alternate, stricter property set (automated) and under AST-based semantic checks.
item_flagging_rules: Flag and log any config that passes verifier but fails AST/semantic equivalence checks.
Flag and log tasks where repair iterations reach max without verifier pass.
Flag pairs with any execution/technical failure for inclusion in exclusion reporting.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Flagged items are analyzed separately and reported as a contamination category; primary analysis excludes technical-failure pairs. Sensitivity analyses include flagged items treated as violations and as non-violations to bound effect.
residual_uncertainty: Residual risk that verifier blind spots remain even after unit tests and stricter re-checks.
Residual risk that passing the deterministic verifier and AST checks does not guarantee production safety in all environments (external-validity).

budget_scenarios.description: Conservative feasibility scenario to demonstrate effect with reduced sample size while preserving paired design.
models: hosted-llm-api (execution manifest will record exact endpoint)
transformations: AST normalization; placeholder substitution; verifier call per iteration
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: N=200 paired tasks; per task: LLM-only 1 call (200), GVR max iterations 4 → up to 5 calls per task (200*5=1000). Total worst-case LLM calls = 1,200. Fits within the maximum model-call budget and reduces wall-clock/time budget.

budget_scenarios.description: Recommended scenario balancing power, budget, and runtime to test a practically meaningful effect size.
models: hosted-llm-api (execution manifest will record exact endpoint)
transformations: AST normalization; placeholder substitution; verifier call per iteration
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: N=400 paired tasks (100 per cluster). Per task: LLM-only single-pass = 1 call → 400 calls. GVR: initial generation + up to 4 repair iterations = up to 5 calls per task → 400*5 = 2,000 calls. Total worst-case calls = 2,400, matching the candidate's earlier estimate and within capability manifest (≤10,000 calls). Deterministic verifier calls do not consume model-call budget.

budget_scenarios.description: Larger sample to explore smaller effect sizes and more fine-grained subgroup analyses.
models: hosted-llm-api (execution manifest will record exact endpoint)
transformations: AST normalization; placeholder substitution; verifier call per iteration
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: N=800 paired tasks. Per-task total worst-case LLM calls = 1 (LLM-only) + 5 (GVR) = 6 → 800*6 = 4,800 LLM calls. Still within maximum planned-model-calls = 10,000 but increases wall-clock time; recommended only if resources/time permit.

power_plan.primary_estimand: Paired difference in probe-level violation proportion (LLM-only minus GVR).
power_plan.target_effect: Absolute reduction of 10 percentage points (e.g., from 20% baseline violation rate under LLM-only to 10% under GVR).
power_plan.calculation_method: Approximate McNemar's test power calculation for paired binary outcomes. Assumptions: baseline paired marginal probabilities consistent with 20% LLM-only violating, 10% GVR violating, discordant pair probabilities implied by those margins; two-sided α=0.05. For these assumptions, N=400 yields estimated power ≈ 0.85–0.95 depending on discordant probability split; N=200 yields power ≈ 0.55–0.75. Calculations will be documented in the execution manifest with exact parameterization and code.
assumptions: Baseline LLM-only violation rate ≈ 20% (conservative, informed by literature C1/C2 but stated as assumption).
GVR reduces violation rate by ≈10 percentage points under the chosen verifier property set.
Pairs are independent across tasks; within-task paired design eliminates between-task variance for the primary outcome.
Discordant pair allocation (LLM-only viol & GVR safe vs. LLM-only safe & GVR viol) is skewed toward improvements (more LLM-only viol & GVR safe).
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With N=400 and McNemar framework, the study is powered to detect ~8–12 percentage-point absolute changes depending on discordant-pair balance; sensitivity analyses will report exact detectable effect across plausible discordant splits.
sensitivity_analyses: Recompute power assuming baseline violation rates of 15% and 25%.
Recompute power under varying discordant pair splits (symmetric vs. asymmetric).
Repeat primary analysis excluding flagged technical-failure pairs and using the conservative imputation options described in missingness_plan.

transformation_families: AST normalization and canonicalization of configurations
Syntactic-to-semantic normalization (e.g., canonical ordering of ACL entries)
semantic_equivalence_checks: AST equality or normalized-AST comparison between original LLM output and repaired output to detect purely syntactic/ordering changes.
Automated semantic checks: for routing/ACL rules, simulate canonical forwarding tables in the verifier and compare intended reachability predicates before and after repair.
automatic_rejection_rules: Automatically reject any generated or repaired config that fails AST/semantic-equivalence normalization checks indicating malformed syntax.
Automatically mark as 'verifier-failed' any config that the deterministic verifier rejects after max iterations; these are reported as unresolved repairs.
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Random 5% of configs that pass the primary verifier are re-evaluated with a stricter property set (automated) and an alternate verification script to estimate residual false negative rates; results automatically logged and summarized.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Deterministic template-to-config mapping code will be unit‑tested on a small public corpus; all mapping code, unit tests, and results recorded in the execution manifest.
residual_risks: Semantic differences that are invisible to AST normalization but relevant in deployment (vendor-specific semantics) remain a residual risk.
Verifier coverage may be incomplete for some policy classes; audit sample aims to quantify but not eliminate this risk.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: External validity to production networks (experiment confined to public templates and deterministic synthetic variations).
Residual verifier blind spots despite unit tests and stricter automated audits.
Possible LLM adaptations that optimize for the verifier oracle rather than for general operational robustness (verifier‑gaming).
Nondeterminism of hosted LLM API responses (recorded via seeds and manifest but may affect reproducibility across vendors/endpoints).
